rationale: Lyc. discourse-introduction verb on the standard ⲡⲉϫⲁϥ pattern, possibly incorporating dative 3pl suffix. Recurs as Kephalaia narrative-frame opener. May alternatively derive from ϫⲛⲉ 'ask, inquire.'
Variant orthography of accumulated ⲙⲁⲛⲭⲟⲣⲉ 'stronghold/fortress' with metathetic/expanded ⲭⲣ→ⲭⲗⲟⲣ cluster. Documents the dialectal variation alongside the existing entry.
Lyc. reflex of ⲟⲩⲱϩⲉ 'cultivated field' (Crum). Used in the agricultural simile of the catechumenate as a tilled land sown by the farmer-apostle.
Lyc. verb apparently identical with ⲡⲱⲱⲛⲉ 'turn, change.' Used here of the beautiful tree's transforming action upon the power of the land — agricultural-cosmological transformation register.

Reduplicated verbal construction in the closing parable-application. Etymology uncertain; possibly Lyc. for a productive/generative verb related to ⲡⲓⲣⲉ 'bring forth' or ⲃⲱⲣⲉ. Confidence low; flagged for parallel attestations.

Idiomatic phrase: ⲙⲧⲁⲛ 'rest' + ⲍⲓ ⲣⲟ 'at the gate/mouth' + ⲉϩⲟⲩⲏⲛ 'inward.' Likely names the inward/secret rest available to catechumens amid outward affliction. Phrase-level idiom requires further attestation for confident rendering.
